sections.title: California annual rotations: cover crop benefits and limits (UC ANR, 2024)
sections.text: UC Cooperative Extension Agronomy Fact Sheet 22 describes cover cropping in California annual crop rotations. Cover crops may reduce erosion and improve soil structure, infiltration and organic matter over time. Benefits depend on species, management and initial soil conditions; short-term carbon or nitrogen increases are not guaranteed. A rapidly closing canopy can suppress weeds growing in the same season. Grasses and brassicas are generally more competitive against weeds than legumes.

sections.title: California cover crops: water, termination and equipment
sections.text: UC ANR advises fitting establishment and termination around the following crop. Winter drought can limit growth; warm-season establishment may require irrigation. Earlier termination during drought may conserve moisture for the cash crop. Terminate before seed set. Methods include mowing, crimping, chemical termination and discing. Residue breakdown commonly requires a 10–30 day gap before planting the next crop; this is not a universal prescription. Seed, machinery and water needs add costs. Some cover crops can host pests or inhibit following crops. This guidance does not quantify a particular farm’s irrigation supply or savings.
